question: The Commission has ordered the compulsory refurbishment of all public buildings in the EU. Can it therefore say which of its own or rented buildings in Brussels and Luxembourg, and those of its delegations and agencies, meet which energy standards? How much will refurbishment cost until single-glazed glass fronts, revolving doors, open garage entrances and draughty gaps between window panes and frames all meet the highest level of insulation it has prescribed?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.6.2024) Since its first Eco-Management and Audit Scheme (EMAS) certification in 2005, the Commission has considerably reduced its energy consumption (-46%1). The technical specifications of the contracts related to buildings contain green criteria, established to meet the Commission’s greening objectives.

In Brussels, the energy performance of the Commission’s office buildings, including those of the executive agencies, is currently around level C, following the scale for public buildings in the Brussels Capital Region. In Luxembourg, six buildings are soon going to be vacated and only two energy performant buildings will remain in 2026.

The Commission is committed to achieve climate neutrality as an organisation by 20302. It aims to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 60% by 20303 and compensate remaining emissions with carbon removals. The real estate strategy aims to cut overall office space by 25% and the number of buildings by 50% by 2030, as well as to improve the environmental impact of the building stock.

Its implementation is well on track in Brussels and Luxembourg. The Commission is releasing buildings to the market for redevelopment towards nearly zeroenergy or zero-emission buildings. Part of the building sales proceeds will be used for costeffective refurbishment projects. The Commission will also prospect for new sustainable and energy performant buildings.

In this sense, the real estate strategy aims to make the Commission fully compliant with the Energy Efficiency Directive4, which states that at least 3% of the total floor area of heated and/or cooled buildings that are owned by public bodies is renovated each year to be transformed into at least nearly zero-energy buildings. The EU Delegations are managed by the European External Action Service (EEAS).
4 Directive (EU) 2023/1791 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 September 2023 on energy
